summaries.demographer: Chol Tran is a 20-year-old Vietnamese American woman born and raised in Portland, Oregon, and currently living in a rented family household with her parents and younger brother in the 97230 area (Q05, Q11, Q86-Q89). She has completed high school coursework but has no diploma and is studying for her GED while working full time as a correctional officer trainee/newer officer (Q65, Q90-Q92). She is never married, has no children, and is not cohabiting with a romantic partner (Q19, Q84). Her household is working-class and multigenerational in responsibility even if not in residence, with shared expenses, immigrant-parent work histories, and strong family obligations (Q55, Q100-Q107).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Chol is motivated by stability, competence, family obligation, and upward mobility, choosing corrections because it offered benefits, training, and a career ladder after leaving school without a diploma (Q02, Q65). She shows high planning behavior through budgeting spreadsheets, automatic savings, shared travel apps, and GED scheduling, but also anxiety-driven monitoring of spending and performance (Q17, Q61, Q83). She is moderately risk-averse financially, able to cover a $400 emergency but sensitive to car, rent, and health costs (Q64, Q82). Peer influence is constructive for her: friends pull her into climbing, basketball, travel, and social routines that balance work stress (Q07, Q32, Q108).
summaries.political_scientist: Chol is a weak-to-moderate Democrat and left-leaning pragmatist, shaped by Portland progressive norms, immigrant-family concerns, and direct corrections experience (Q24, Q95, Q96). She votes by mail and pays particular attention to local issues such as housing, public safety, schools, health care, racism, and immigrant communities (Q23, Q24). Her institutional trust is conditional: she respects public safety work but emphasizes documentation, accountability, de-escalation, language access, and procedural fairness (Q20, Q25-Q27). She engages politically through discussion and careful information-seeking more than protest or online argument (Q29, Q30, Q48).
summaries.psychologist: Chol presents as conscientious, competitive, socially connected, and achievement-oriented, with a strong need to prove competence after educational disruption (Q01-Q03, Q43). Her anxiety shows up as over-analysis, replaying work incidents, checking details, and worry about family, money, and performance, but she has developed structured coping routines including yoga, journaling, breathing, exercise, and trusted conversations (Q43-Q45, Q50). She balances collectivist family loyalty with emerging independence, often acting as translator, helper, and role model while wanting her own space (Q05, Q11, Q108). Her self-concept centers on reliability, fairness, growth, and not being defined by one unfinished credential (Q109).
